scope: The IntelliJ read pipeline and the file reads: admission and cancellation through CallAdmission, committed-document read computations, indexing readiness with the bounded wait, sanitized failures, fixed failure precedence, path resolution, read_file and find_file. Depends on CAP-READ-DOMAIN. Wire JSON argument parsing, tool schemas, the LLM status/code/content envelope and rendering of read outcomes into ToolOutcome content are excluded and belong to the codec feature.

requirements.statement: read_file takes a path, an optional 1-based start line (default 1) and an optional 1-based inclusive end line (default start plus 99). An end before start, or a span above 300 lines, is an argument rejection. Lines are the lines of the current document text with LF terminators; a final LF does not start another line, and an empty document has zero lines. The range is clipped at end of file and the actual range is returned. A start line after the last line, including any start in an empty document, returns RANGE_OUT_OF_BOUNDS with the line count. The 24 KiB cap counts the UTF-8 bytes of the returned lines including their LF terminators. When the cap cuts the range, the result holds the largest whole-line prefix, its actual range and a truncated flag. When the start line alone exceeds 24 KiB, the result is LINE_EXCEEDS_BYTE_CAP with that line's byte size. A binary file, or a file the platform does not load as text content, returns UNSUPPORTED_FILE. A successful read returns a read handle.

A path argument is relative to the project base directory or absolute. The adapter normalizes it (removes '.' and '..' segments, resolves symbolic links) before any check. Project content roots, library source roots, excluded roots and the project base directory are compared in the same canonical form, with symbolic links resolved. The first matching check wins, in this order: (1) the normalized path is not under a project content root or an attached library source root, decided by its nearest existing ancestor, returns OUTSIDE_PROJECT; a file in a library class root (compiled classes) is OUTSIDE_PROJECT; (2) the path is under an excluded root returns EXCLUDED_PATH; (3) no file or directory exists returns FILE_NOT_FOUND; (4) a directory where a file is required returns NOT_A_FILE. A returned path is rendered with '/' separators relative to the canonical project base directory when the file is under it, and otherwise as the platform file URL (for example a jar:// URL for a library source entry); both forms are accepted as path input. Library files are read-only evidence.

find_file takes a query and a scope. The query is an exact case-sensitive file name, or a relative path of one or more whole trailing path segments ending in a file name, matched case-sensitively ('a/B.java' matches '…/a/B.java' and not '…/xa/B.java'). Scope PROJECT (default) covers non-excluded project content except generated sources. Scope LIBRARIES covers PROJECT content plus attached library sources. A generated source is a file for which any GeneratedSourcesFilter reports generated. Each result carries its rendered path (SR-004) and origin PROJECT or LIBRARY. Results are ordered by rendered path. Paged collection applies the result collection cap (SR-002): more results than the cap returns TOO_MANY_RESULTS with a narrowing hint and no page.

Current editor content is authoritative. Every operation computes its result inside one read computation that runs only when all documents are committed (the platform documents-committed constraint), so every returned text and range comes from the current document including unsaved changes, and every PSI range matches the reported document version. The document version is the document modification stamp.

Index-backed operations (find_file, search_symbols, get_symbol_info, find_references, search_text) run their read computation under the platform smart-mode constraint, and every index-backed platform call, including reference search, runs inside that read computation and never outside read access. The total wait for smart mode, including restarts after dumb mode begins during the computation, is bounded by the index wait bound: an injected duration with production value 30 seconds. DumbService.waitForSmartMode(long) is not used. At the bound the operation returns INDEX_NOT_READY with a retry hint and no partial result. An IndexNotReadyException that escapes the computation also returns INDEX_NOT_READY with no partial result. A write action that cancels a read computation restarts it; time spent in these restarts does not count toward the index wait bound and has no bound, and only cancellation (SR-019) ends it. read_file and get_file_outline do not wait for indexing. A closed, disposed or not-yet-initialized project returns PROJECT_UNAVAILABLE. No operation returns an empty success because indexes were unavailable.

Each read is one admitted executable call. The read executor receives the CallAdmission and RunCancellation that the ToolRunner passes and calls CallAdmission.execute exactly once off the EDT. When execute returns Limited or Rejected, the Effect did not run, no IntelliJ access happens, and the read executor returns a typed NotAdmitted result that carries the admission result; the codec feature maps it to ToolOutcome.NotStarted with RUN_LIMIT_NOT_STARTED for Limited and CANCELLED_NOT_STARTED for Rejected. The Effect contains the index wait and the whole read computation, and it returns or throws only after the platform read computation for this call has terminated. The run cancellation token cancels the wait and the computation; the listener registered on RunCancellation only requests that cancellation and never blocks, because RunSession runs listeners under its monitor, possibly on the EDT. On cancellation, including content close, the Effect throws java.util.concurrent.CancellationException, so the lifecycle records FAILED_AFTER_START and the frozen driver records ToolOutcome.FailedAfterStart with no touched paths; no success value, partial result, handle or page token is produced. Handles and page tokens are registered only after the computation completed without cancellation. If the registry is disposed when they are registered, it registers nothing and the Effect throws java.util.concurrent.CancellationException with the same lifecycle and driver results. Expected read outcomes return normally. The read never waits for the EDT while it holds read access.

An unexpected platform failure during a read returns READ_FAILED with a category from a closed set and no source text, arguments or stack content. The first matching rule gives the category: PATH_RESOLUTION for a failure in the SR-004 path checks; INDEX_QUERY for a failure inside a name index, file name index or reference search call; DOCUMENT_READ for a failure while reading document text or line offsets; PSI_READ for every other failure at SR-026 steps 2 to 9. A violated domain invariant throws. Logs record only operation, category and counts. Every outcome that carries a hint (STALE_HANDLE, STALE_PAGE, INDEX_NOT_READY, TOO_MANY_RESULTS, SOURCE_TOO_LARGE, LINE_EXCEEDS_BYTE_CAP, UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE, READ_FAILED) names only catalog tools. The UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE hint names read_file and search_text as the labeled fallback.

Failure precedence for one admitted read, first applicable wins: (1) cancellation, including a disposed registry at registration (SR-019); (2) PROJECT_UNAVAILABLE; (3) registry lookup of an input symbol handle, including an owner type handle (STALE_HANDLE), then of an input page token, including a different operation or argument set (STALE_PAGE), then the PSI modification count of the token (STALE_PAGE), all without waiting for indexing; (4) path outcomes in SR-004 order; (5) file-type and language outcomes (UNSUPPORTED_FILE, UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE), without waiting for indexing; (6) INDEX_NOT_READY for index-backed operations; (7) re-resolution STALE_HANDLE (SR-013), then NOT_A_TYPE (SR-006), then PSI modification count STALE_PAGE inside the operation computation (SR-017); (8) TOO_MANY_RESULTS; (9) the operation result, including RANGE_OUT_OF_BOUNDS, LINE_EXCEEDS_BYTE_CAP and SOURCE_TOO_LARGE. An unexpected platform failure at steps 2 to 9 returns READ_FAILED. Argument rejection (SR-001) happens before admission. The read pipeline has all nine steps from this slice on; steps whose outcomes belong to later slices (STALE_HANDLE and NOT_A_TYPE in read-symbols, STALE_PAGE in read-text-search) stay in their positions and are bound by those slices without a change to this order.

acceptance.when: In a fixture project with lines of exactly 10 KiB plus LF, read_file lines 1–5 of that file, a range across end of file, a start after end of file, an empty file, a file whose first line exceeds 24 KiB, a binary file, a text file above the content-loading limit, a directory, a missing project path, a missing path under an excluded directory, an existing excluded file, a missing and an existing absolute path outside the project, a symlink inside the project that points outside it, a non-Java text file by absolute path, a library source file by its jar URL and a class file in a library class root; separately, in a fixture whose project base directory is reached through a symbolic link, read_file a project file by its relative path and by its absolute path through the link.
acceptance.then: Lines 1–5 return exactly lines 1–2 with actual range 1–2 and truncated set; the end-of-file range is clipped to the last line; the empty file and the late start return RANGE_OUT_OF_BOUNDS with their line counts; LINE_EXCEEDS_BYTE_CAP is returned with the first line's exact byte size; the binary file and the file above the content-loading limit return UNSUPPORTED_FILE; the directory returns NOT_A_FILE; the missing project path returns FILE_NOT_FOUND; both excluded cases return EXCLUDED_PATH; both outside paths, the symlink and the class file return OUTSIDE_PROJECT; the text file and the library source succeed; the symlinked-base reads succeed and render the same '/'-separated path relative to the project base directory; successful reads return read handles with the observed version.

acceptance.when: Run find_file for a name present in source, generated source, an excluded directory and a library source, with PROJECT and LIBRARIES scopes; also run find_file for 'a/B.java' where 'a/B.java' and 'xa/B.java' exist. With the result collection cap injected as 2, run find_file for a name present in 3 project files.
acceptance.then: PROJECT returns only the source file with origin PROJECT; LIBRARIES returns exactly the source file and the library file with their origins; the source file renders as its '/'-separated path relative to the project base directory and the library file as its jar URL; generated and excluded files are absent; paths are ordered; the suffix query returns only 'a/B.java'. The capped query returns TOO_MANY_RESULTS with a narrowing hint and no page.

acceptance.when: With the index wait bound injected as 200 ms, enter dumb mode through the platform dumb-mode test utility and call find_file; call find_file again and leave dumb mode before the bound; call read_file during dumb mode.
acceptance.then: The first call returns INDEX_NOT_READY with a catalog-only retry hint and no results after at least 200 ms; the second call returns results after indexing ends; read_file succeeds without waiting.

acceptance.when: Stop the run from the EDT while a find_file read waits for indexing, and while a find_file computation blocks inside a test GeneratedSourcesFilter on a latch that the test releases only after Stop; separately close the content while such a read blocks; separately dispose the registry, without cancelling the run, while a find_file computation with limit 1 over two matching files blocks on such a latch; separately run a read whose CallAdmission returns Limited and one whose CallAdmission returns Rejected.
acceptance.then: Each cancelled or disposed call's admission status is FAILED_AFTER_START, the Effect threw java.util.concurrent.CancellationException, and the driver records ToolOutcome.FailedAfterStart with no touched paths; Stop returned before the latch was released; the Effect returned only after the blocked computation terminated; no page token was registered; admission counted each read once; the read computation thread and the Effect calling thread were not the EDT; the Limited and Rejected reads return NotAdmitted with their admission result and made no IntelliJ call.

acceptance.when: Make a read adapter throw an unexpected platform exception containing source text and a path, once during path checks, once inside a test GeneratedSourcesFilter during find_file and once while reading document lines for read_file.
acceptance.then: The operation returns READ_FAILED with categories PATH_RESOLUTION, PSI_READ and DOCUMENT_READ in that order; the outcome and captured log contain no source text, argument or stack content.

acceptance.when: In dumb mode with the index wait bound injected as 200 ms, call read_file with a missing path under an excluded directory and on a binary file; with a closed project, call read_file and find_file; make path resolution throw an unexpected platform exception.
acceptance.then: read_file returns EXCLUDED_PATH and UNSUPPORTED_FILE before 200 ms elapse; both closed-project calls return PROJECT_UNAVAILABLE; the injected failure returns READ_FAILED with category PATH_RESOLUTION.

acceptance.when: Open a text file in an editor and change one line without saving, then call read_file for that line and find_file for the file name.
acceptance.then: read_file returns the unsaved line text and the unsaved document version; find_file returns the file.

type_safety_audit.invalid: Partial lines, a silently empty read, invented ranges, an over-span request, or binary bytes returned as text
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Argument factory applies line defaults and rejects end before start and spans above 300; operation-local read_file outcome variants for success with actual range, range out of bounds, line cap exceeded and unsupported file
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter computes line offsets on the document text observed in one read action
type_safety_audit.justification: Line structure and file type are runtime properties of the document

type_safety_audit.invalid: A read of an arbitrary filesystem path or of an excluded tree
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Validated path argument plus a sealed path-resolution outcome whose variants follow the fixed check order; resolved file identity is constructible only by the adapter
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter normalizes the path, resolves symbolic links and checks project file index membership under read access in the SR-004 order
type_safety_audit.justification: Filesystem layout and project roots are mutable external state

type_safety_audit.invalid: Excluded or generated files in PROJECT results, or library files without an explicit scope
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Scope enum with PROJECT default; result entries carry rendered path (SR-004) and origin
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter filters excluded and generated files with platform file index checks

type_safety_audit.invalid: A result built from disk text while an editor holds unsaved changes, or PSI ranges from an uncommitted document
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Result values carry the document version they were computed against
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter runs every read computation under the documents-committed constraint
type_safety_audit.justification: Unsaved state exists only in the running IDE (I6)

type_safety_audit.invalid: An authoritative empty result during indexing, or an unbounded wait
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Sealed readiness outcome shared by index-backed operations; the index wait bound is a validated injected positive duration
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter runs index-backed platform calls only inside the smart-mode read computation with the bound and maps index-not-ready failures
type_safety_audit.justification: Indexing state changes at runtime and has no partial-result signal on the platform

type_safety_audit.invalid: A read that bypasses admission, blocks the EDT, returns while its computation still runs, registers handles after Stop or disposal, reports partial results after Stop, or returns a completed result when admission refused
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Read executor accepts only a CallAdmission and a RunCancellation and returns a sealed read execution result with operation-local outcome variants and a NotAdmitted variant carrying the admission result; handle registration happens after the computation result is obtained
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter links the run cancellation token to the platform read computation with a nonblocking listener, awaits termination on the Effect thread, and throws java.util.concurrent.CancellationException on cancellation or a disposed registry
type_safety_audit.justification: Thread and cancellation behavior are runtime properties (I7, I8)

type_safety_audit.invalid: A swallowed platform exception reported as success, or source text in a log
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: READ_FAILED variant with a closed category enum and no free-form content; hint values are built only from catalog tool names; invariant checks throw
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter catches platform exceptions at the boundary and maps them with the SR-020 category rule
type_safety_audit.justification: Platform failures are external; I10 forbids content in logs

type_safety_audit.invalid: Two possible outcomes for one call, or a wait for indexing before a registry or path failure
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: One adapter pipeline with ordered stages, each returning a sealed stage outcome that short-circuits
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter maps unexpected platform failures to READ_FAILED at each stage
type_safety_audit.justification: Deterministic outcomes are a workflow principle; the model must receive the same failure for the same state

non_goals: Wire JSON argument parsing, tool schemas, tool descriptions, the LLM status/code/content envelope and ToolOutcome content rendering
Mutations, handle invalidation on agent edits, formatting, diagnostics, build and test execution
Regex search, case-insensitive search, glob file patterns and whole-project unscoped text search
Semantic support or parity claims for languages other than Java
Session owner wiring, New Session UI and tool-window content lifetime integration beyond a registry dispose operation
Persisting handles, page tokens or read results across sessions
MCP, HTTP, idea-facade or any second index beside IntelliJ
Changing CAP-LIFECYCLE-ADMISSION or CAP-DOMAIN-RUN-DRIVER declarations or semantics
Requirements, operations and acceptance owned by the other semantic reads slices
assumptions: Requirement IDs are unique across the five semantic reads slices, which replace CAP-SEMANTIC-READS. A reference to a requirement outside this spec names the slice that owns it: read-domain SR-001, SR-002, SR-012, SR-014, SR-021, SR-022, SR-023, SR-024; read-pipeline SR-003, SR-004, SR-005, SR-015, SR-016, SR-019, SR-020, SR-026; read-text-search SR-010, SR-017; read-symbols SR-006, SR-007, SR-008, SR-011, SR-013, SR-018, SR-025; read-references SR-009, SR-027.

CAP-LIFECYCLE-ADMISSION is frozen with FINAL_GATE_PASS; its S3 is blocked only on EV-SURFACE. This feature relies on its admission semantics, and this feature's S3 cannot close while lifecycle S3 remains blocked.
CAP-DOMAIN-RUN-DRIVER is closed; reads bind to its PlannedCall.ToolOperation, ToolRunner and CallAdmission surfaces without changing them.

A read cancelled after admission, or finding a disposed registry at registration, throws java.util.concurrent.CancellationException from the Effect; the frozen driver maps it to ToolOutcome.FailedAfterStart with the message 'Tool execution failed after admission: CancellationException' and no touched paths (NativeRunDriver.executeOne). The frozen driver acts on the ToolRunner's returned NotStarted reason for refused admission (NativeRunDriver.kt:156-179), so the codec maps the NotAdmitted read result as SR-019 states. The codec feature renders expected read outcomes into ToolOutcome content and cannot change lifecycle accounting.

IntelliJ JUnit 5 test fixtures for a Java project with editors, libraries, generated and excluded roots, dumb mode and a test reference query executor are available through the IntelliJ Platform Gradle test framework configuration; the design may change plugin-core/build.gradle.kts for this and must keep tests discoverable as @Test methods.

Name and file indexes throw IndexNotReadyException in dumb mode (FileBasedIndexImpl). Reference search executors that are not dumb-aware block until smart mode when called without read access (QueryExecutorBase.java:57-66), so SR-016 requires calls inside the read computation. Dumb-mode entry runs a write action (DumbServiceImpl.kt:335-342), and a write action cancels a running non-blocking read computation, which reruns only when its constraints hold again (NonBlockingReadActionImpl.java:639-641,808-814). The platform exposes no partial-result signal for reference search; completeness is only complete or more results.

Only the document modification stamp changes on unsaved edits; the view provider stamp stays at the last committed stamp. The PSI modification count changes on committed physical PSI changes and on dumb-mode entry and exit, not on uncommitted edits.

Normalizations of product bounds: limit 1–100 with default 50 for find_references; 300 lines and 24 KiB for get_symbol_info source with SOURCE_TOO_LARGE above it; 1,000 UTF-16 units for text queries; LINE_EXCEEDS_BYTE_CAP as the explicit error for a start line above 24 KiB (product 'smaller read or explicit unsupported error').

Normalizations of product terms: SR-025 range, signature, owner and containing-declaration definitions; SR-006 catalog declaration kinds; SR-003 line model and defaults; SR-004 path rendering and check order; SR-010 match and excerpt rule and skipped-file count; SR-020 READ_FAILED category rule; SR-026 failure precedence; SR-001 query validation; SR-004 canonical root comparison; SR-009 reference range, line and kind; SR-010 document offsets and match column; SR-025 parameter type text, array dimensions and compact constructors; SR-012 entry kinds.

Normalizations of scope: generated sources are omitted from find_file, unrestricted search_symbols and search_text directory scans, and included and marked in find_references so reference sets stay complete; handle reuse for the same element (SR-011) keeps one live handle per element in the registry.
The product rule 'reports partial search/index readiness separately' is satisfied by fail-closed INDEX_NOT_READY and TOO_MANY_RESULTS outcomes, because the platform gives no partial-result signal.

The PSI modification count also changes for document and VFS changes to project-content files whose PSI is not loaded (PsiDocumentManagerBase.java:1149,1314; PsiVFSListener.java:139-148), so SR-017 staleness covers find_file and search_text over unloaded files.
